summary: Duplicate pending tags: 103 (chunk, concept) pairs proposed by both Carnice-9b and Qwen3.5-27B, creating double-review burden for identical propositions

analysis.author: corpus-quality
analysis.content:
SWEPT 2026-08-20: Query on data/guru.db found 103 (chunk_id, concept_id) pairs where BOTH 'pending' and from DIFFERENT models:

Models producing duplicate pending:
- Carnic-9b + Qwen3.5-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf: all 103 pairs

This is legal by the current unique index idx_staged_tags_provenance_unique = UNIQUE(chunk_id, concept_id, model, prompt_version) WHERE status='pending' — since model is part of the key, both inserts succeed.

Top affected texts:
- christian_mysticism.life-and-doctrines-boehme: 64 dup pairs (worst hit)
- mesopotamian.enuma-elish: 26 dup pairs
- buddhism.diamond-sutra: 12 dup pairs
- gnosticism.gospel-of-thomas: 1 dup pair

All 103 cases are the SAME concept proposed by both models (just different model provenance), not different concepts. The resolutions are both pending; neither has been reviewed.

OVERLAP: Ticket 56d6d337 already documents this exact mechanism and query. This intake confirms the scope has grown: the ticket was filed 2026-08-09, and the sweep shows 103 pairs (not resolved).

analysis.author: corpus-quality
analysis.content:
INVESTIGATED (2026-08-20): The 103 'duplicate pending tags' are NOT a bug — they are legitimate multi-model proposals.

103 pairs of (chunk, concept) pending from different models:
- 77 pairs: Carnice-9b + Qwen3.5-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf (both v1)
- 26 pairs: Qwen3.5 + qwen-3-4b-guru-v3 (v3 prompt)

By source text: christian_mysticism 64, mesopotamian 26, buddhism 12, gnosticism 1.

The unique index on staged_tags is (chunk_id, concept_id, model, prompt_version) — so two different models producing the same (chunk, concept) is BY DESIGN, not a violation. The staged_tags schema explicitly supports multi-model batches (two model batches CAN legally produce two pending rows for the same chunk+concept — this is the 'duplicate-pending-tags' scenario by construction, per the corpus-quality docs).

These are NOT curator-fixable duplicates — they are pending tags awaiting normal review (accept/reject). The 'duplicate' represents inter-model agreement (both models proposed the same tag), which is actually useful signal for the reviewer.

This ticket should be RECLASSIFIED as 'expected behavior' or downgraded to 'info' — there's nothing to fix. The 206 rows across 103 pairs are all legitimately pending for review in the normal tag queue.
